headline: No Permit Required for Nova Scotia Coastal Entry
reservation: This is a day-use provincial park with no entry permits or reservations required for beach access. There is no overnight camping permitted within the park boundaries. Nearby private accommodations should be booked well in advance during the summer surf season.

days.title: Atlantic Surf and Cobble Beach

stops.name: Lawrencetown Beach Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk the supervised swimming area and observe the world-class swell that attracts surfers year-round.

stops.name: Atlantic View Trail
stops.detail: Utilize this multi-use rail trail that runs behind the beach for a view of the coastal salt marshes.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes from downtown Halifax; conditions vary.
days.note: Strong rip currents are common; swimming is only recommended in supervised areas during posted lifeguard hours.

days.title: Coastal Headlands and Wildlife

stops.name: Conrads Beach
stops.detail: Visit this nearby protected area, known for its piping plover nesting sites and calmer waters.

stops.name: Lawrencetown Head
stops.detail: View the dramatic erosion of the drumlin cliffs that flank the eastern end of the main beach.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes between local beach points; conditions vary.
days.note: Respect all seasonal cordoned-off areas on the dunes designed to protect endangered bird nesting sites.

days.title: The Eastern Shore Loop

stops.name: Fisherman's Cove
stops.detail: A short drive back toward the harbor to explore a restored 200-year-old fishing village with local craft shops.

stops.name: Hope for Wildlife
stops.detail: Visit the nearby rehabilitation centre to learn about local maritime fauna conservation efforts.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for the loop; conditions vary.
days.note: Check the tide charts locally as the beach width and surf conditions change dramatically between high and low tide.

intel.title: Peak Beach Demand
intel.text: The primary paved lot fills to capacity by noon on sunny summer weekends. Arrive early or plan a midweek visit to ensure a space in the designated park areas.

intel.title: Urban Proximity
intel.text: Cellular signal is generally strong throughout Lawrencetown due to its proximity to Dartmouth. However, reception can drop behind the high dunes or along the rail trail.

intel.title: Local Services
intel.text: Fuel and convenience stores are available in the community of Lawrencetown and along Route 207. No services are located directly on the beach sand.

intel.title: Lifeguard Season
intel.text: Supervised swimming is typically limited to July and August. Outside of these months, the beach remains open for walking and surfing, but at your own risk.

intel.title: Public Transit
intel.text: While predominantly a vehicle-access park, seasonal shuttle options from the city sometimes exist. Verify the current Halifax Transit seasonal schedule for the Route 401 connection.

plan.arrival: Collect a rental car at YHZ airport and drive south via Highway 107; stop in Dartmouth for a full beach kit and supplies before reaching the coast.
plan.vehicle: Compact cars are ideal for the narrow coastal roads and smaller parking stalls found along the Eastern Shore.
plan.goldenHour: The eastern cliffs at Lawrencetown Head provide a striking backdrop for sunrise, while the western end captures the late afternoon glow over the Atlantic.
